title: 21st sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with 54 members present. Members questioned the Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy about stalled Fenaka power projects on several islands, power cuts in Addu City, erosion and waste management. They then held the preliminary debate on a government bill to hold council by-elections within 183 days instead of 60; most speakers backed it, a few questioned its priority or its effect on representation. Debate on a legal profession bill closed and a debate on the Employment Act amendment was under way when this part ended. This part opens partway through a member's speech on the bill amending the Employment Act, which calls on the Labour Minister to enforce existing worker rights, asks for rest-day, overtime and probation protections to be strengthened, and says migrant workers' rights must be fully respected. The Majlis then took up the Finance Committee's report on the nominee for Maldives Monetary Authority Governor, which the committee said scored 94.43% in its assessment; two members spoke on it. After a break, the Majlis held three votes: it accepted for committee review a bill amending the Decentralisation Act (84-0, sent to the Decentralisation Committee) and a bill amending the Legal Profession Act (83-0, sent to the Judiciary Committee), and approved advising the President to appoint Ahmed Munawar as MMA Governor (78-0). The sitting closed with the next one set for Wednesday 31 July 2024 at 9:00.

items.title: Advice to the President on appointing the MMA Governor (Ahmed Munawar)

speakers.name: Thoriq Ibrahim (Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy)
positions: Said Fenaka's Kendhoo powerhouse is stalled for lack of funds and could finish in about six months once funded.
Said Addu City has 20 MW of generators with some broken; a new 1.5 MW unit and repairs due this year.
Said coastal studies and a vulnerability index are under way; the sandbank area is to be managed from December.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked when the stalled Fenaka powerhouse in Kendhoo will be completed, and raised Kudarikilu, Kihadhoo, Kamadhoo plots and Fenaka staff contracts.
Raised a point of order that the chair rejected as promoting a party.
On the Employment Act bill, said enforcement agencies lag in applying the law.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Raised a point of order on the chair's remarks to members and the minister; the chair did not accept it.
Asked what is being done now and long term about Addu City's electricity problem.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Asked about delays at the Thulusdhoo landfill contractor and how contractors who stall are chosen and removed.
Raised a point of order on by-election timing; the chair did not accept it.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Introduced the government bill: hold by-elections within 183 days to cut repeated election costs.
Closing remarks: about half of by-elections are uncontested with low turnout; asked that the bill go to committee.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the bill; said committee should ensure no by-election when a council keeps its quorum.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Argued cost saving is not the main aim and doubted the amendment brings meaningful savings or is a priority.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: Asked how soon erosion on islands in his constituency will be fixed and whether the EPA has rules for the protected sandbank area.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Noted the Kendhoo project's cost rose and it is unfinished; asked whether work given to non-performing contractors can be taken over.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Asked whether the former minister should answer for costly unfinished powerhouse projects, and who is accountable now.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked about plans for Kulhudhuffushi's Fenaka building, extra capacity, the MWSC relocation timeline and the solar project.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Asked what became of MVR 26 million spent on the Madaveli powerhouse and when the problem for nearby residents will be resolved.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when Vaikaradhoo's largely built powerhouse will begin supplying electricity.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked when work to fix Thulhaadhoo's low-voltage supply will actually start.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked about islands managing waste well, Hoarafushi's erosion, WAMCO's payroll growth and water and sewerage projects.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked how far the Maduvvari electricity upgrade has progressed and when the Fenaka building at Meedhoo will be finished.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the bill, citing election cost savings and better integrity and participation.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the amendment is not a priority now, urged revenue-raising bills instead and asked for it to be withdrawn.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill and fewer council elections; said some councillors underperform and council spending needs review.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill but warned of a loophole where resignations could trigger elections; urged committee changes.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Supported the bill as a saving for councils and residents; said quorum rules need care.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Supported the bill and cutting councillor numbers to reduce state spending.

speakers.name: Adam Zahir
positions: Supported the bill, saying about half of by-elections are uncontested and turnout is low; cited Elections Commission cost concerns.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Did not back the bill as drafted over lost representation, e.g. in Addu City council; would support if fixed in committee.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill but said councillor numbers should not be cut only to save money; frequent by-elections are unnecessary.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: As sponsor of the legal profession bill, urged committee to consult Islamic-law scholars on lawyers' Sharia training.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shamin Habeeb
positions: On the Employment Act bill, urged that foreign workers work only for their permit holder and regulations be strengthened.

speakers.name: Qasim Ibrahim
positions: As committee rapporteur, presented the Finance Committee report recommending the nominee for MMA Governor, who scored 94.43% against the 75% pass mark.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Said senior state appointments should be made with honesty and sincerity, and welcomed that the government is choosing people with education and experience.

decisions: Preliminary debate on the Decentralisation Act amendment (by-elections within 183 days) closed; vote set for voting time.
Preliminary debate on the Legal Profession Act amendment closed; vote set for voting time.
The bill amending the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) was accepted by the Majlis and sent to the Decentralisation Committee.
The bill amending the Legal Profession Act (Law 5/2019) was accepted by the Majlis and sent to the Judiciary Committee.
The Majlis approved advising the President to appoint Ahmed Munawar as Governor of the Maldives Monetary Authority.
The sitting closed; the next sitting was set for Wednesday 31 July 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the bill amending the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) for committee review
Accept the bill amending the Legal Profession Act (Law 5/2019) for committee review
Advise the President to appoint Ahmed Munawar as MMA Governor
